MEET EMELIE

About Emelie

I am a fully insured and qualified BEVA/BVDA equine dental technician and member of the British Association of Equine Dental Technicians (BAEDT), providing a professional, knowledgeable and reliable service to all equines across the South West.

I work with competition horses, happy hackers, and welfare and charity cases of all shapes, ages and sizes. My aim is to provide a pleasant and educational visit for both horse and owner.

Alongside this, I'm also a Registered Veterinary Nurse with over 16 years of clinical experience, which has given me an extensive understanding of horse behaviour. If your horse requires sedation, I'm happy to liaise with your vet to arrange a suitable plan.

ROUTINE DENTAL CARE

When should my horse see an Equine Dental Technician?

Discuss your horse’s dental care ↗

Routine dental care is an essential part of your horse’s overall health and welfare. Every horse should have a dental examination at least once every 12 months, although some horses may require more frequent checks depending on their age, dental condition and individual needs.

Dental problems are rarely obvious from the outside, and horses are naturally inclined to continue eating and performing despite significant discomfort or even severe problems within the mouth. Regular dental examinations with a BAEDT technician can help identify issues early, before they develop into more serious problems.

Poor dental health can affect your horse in several ways, including difficulty chewing, quidding (dropping partially chewed food), weight loss, bit resistance, ridden discomfort and changes in behaviour. Regular checks help maintain comfortable, efficient chewing and support your horse’s long-term health and wellbeing.

Following your horse’s initial examination, I will recommend an individual dental maintenance plan, depending on their age, dental condition and ongoing needs. This ensures your horse receives appropriate care tailored to them.

AT YOUR APPOINTMENT

What to expect at your horse’s routine dental appointment

Every dental appointment is carried out with your horse’s welfare and comfort in mind. I take a thorough, individual approach to each examination to ensure any findings are identified, explained and appropriately addressed. Appointments usually take 30 to 45 minutes.

01

Discussion of your horse’s history

We will begin by discussing your horse’s dental history, general health, age, diet and any concerns you may have noticed, including changes in eating, behaviour or ridden performance.

02

External examination

Your horse’s overall condition and head will be assessed, followed by an external examination of the lips and incisors. This helps identify any visible abnormalities or signs that may require further investigation.

03

Thorough oral examination

A dental speculum will be carefully fitted to allow the mouth to be examined safely and thoroughly. Your horse’s mouth will be rinsed so I can see clearly. Using appropriate lighting, dental mirrors, picks and probes, I will assess the oral cavity, including the cheek teeth, tongue and surrounding soft tissues, looking for abnormalities or signs of dental disease. Your horse will be given breaks with their mouth closed during the examination.

04

Findings and treatment plan

All findings are recorded and assessed, allowing an appropriate treatment plan to be developed for your horse. I will explain any abnormalities identified and discuss the recommended treatment with you before proceeding.

05

Dental treatment

The necessary dental treatment is then carried out using a variety of tools Powerfloats, hand rasps, picks, flushing tools - to suit your horse’s individual needs, with an emphasis on comfort, safety, welfare and maintaining good oral health.

06

Dental chart and records

Following the appointment, a digital dental chart documenting the examination findings and treatment performed will be completed and emailed to you for your records. This provides a useful record of your horse’s dental health and helps inform future maintenance and treatment recommendations. Your invoice will be attached to the chart and an appointment will be made for the next visit at an appropriate recall time, based on the findings.

My aim is to ensure every owner understands their horse’s dental health, with clear explanations and recommendations tailored to the individual horse.

COMMON QUESTIONS

Before you book.

Where does Real Equine Dentistry offer appointments?

Real Equine Dentistry is based in East Devon and covers the South West. Contact Emelie to arrange a visit to your horse.

How often should my horse have a dental examination?

Every horse should have a dental examination at least once every 12 months. Some horses need more frequent checks depending on their age, dental condition and individual needs. Emelie will recommend a suitable interval after the examination.

How long does a horse’s dental appointment take?

A routine dental appointment usually takes 30 to 45 minutes. This includes discussing your horse’s history, examining the mouth, explaining the findings and carrying out the appropriate treatment.

What if my horse needs sedation?

If your horse needs sedation, Emelie can liaise with your vet to arrange a suitable plan. Please mention any previous sedation requirements when booking.

How do I book an equine dental appointment?

Complete the booking form to request an appointment. You can also call Emelie on 07969 420088, send a WhatsApp message or email realequinedentistry@outlook.com.
